paper.title_en: Scalar Black-Holes in Gravity from Entropy
paper.abstract_en: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black holes in Gravity from Entropy (GfE), focusing on the sector in which the bosonic form-space field is a pure scalar. Starting from the full auxiliary-field equations, we show that the Dirac--Kähler matter equation contains both a scalar equation and a two-form consistency condition. The latter is automatically satisfied by a radial scalar. We derive an exact integral identity, valid for a general backreacted static spherical geometry, and prove that a regular scalar approaching zero at infinity must vanish if the sampled scalar and radial auxiliary-field eigenvalues are positive and the effective mass squared $m^2+ξR$ is nonnegative. In particular, this excludes minimally coupled static scalar hair with $m^2\geq0$ on the regular identity-connected branch. We also present the perturbative GfE vacuum geometry and use its curvature to identify the region in which nonminimal coupling can evade the sign argument. A second, sharper estimate shows that making $m^2+ξR$ negative is not by itself sufficient to produce a regular static zero mode: a finite interval of nonminimal couplings still admits no branch bifurcating from the vacuum solution.
